sources.title: Albert E. Dien, Eastern Wei and Northern Qi, The Cambridge History of China 2 (2019)
sources.note: Publisher abstract directly read; original chapter pp. 191-197 read in full at https://dokumen.pub/the-cambridge-history-of-china-volume-2-the-six-dynasties-220-589-1107020778-9781107020771.html . DOI 10.1017/9781139107334.011. History and moving-city/granary passages stay within a single conservative 200-word budget for the chapter and mirror.

sources.title: Soojung Han, Empress Dowager Lou the Kingmaker (2025)
sources.note: Original scholarly article directly read, opening biographical discussion and conclusion. Only earlier support for Gao Huan is used; subsequent Northern Qi institutions are not assigned to Eastern Wei. No Princess Linhe/Ruru tomb material used.

sources.title: Francesca Bray, Agriculture, The Cambridge History of China 2 (2019)
sources.note: Publisher chapter summary directly read: Qimin yaoshu completed 533-544; Jia Sixie a practising farmer, estate owner and former middle-ranking Northern Wei official. No claim of an Eastern Wei state commission. Separate original chapter, not derived from the book mirror.

sources.title: Jin-Xiu Wang, Tian-Gang Gao and Sandra Knapp, Ancient Chinese Literature Reveals Pathways of Eggplant Domestication (2008)
sources.note: Original Annals of Botany paper, sections Size and Taste, read through indexed original after direct PMC challenge. Reproducible query: "Ancient Chinese Literature" "small beans". The early sixth-century text compares size with a pellet and flavour with small beans. Later medieval improvements are not projected backward.

sources.title: Wang Hui, Drinks in Chinese material and food history, published book excerpt (2024)
sources.note: Direct government-hosted excerpt of 王辉, 宴飨万年：文物中的中华饮食文化史, Guangxi People’s Publishing House, 2024. Paragraph beginning 同时，《齐民要术》. Only the concrete sour-jujube processing recipe is used; other broad first-in-world and medical claims on this page are not adopted.

sources.title: Kate Lingley, Patron and Community in Eastern Wei Shanxi: The Gaomiaoshan Cave Temple Yi-Society (2010)
sources.note: Original Asia Major 23.1, pp. 127-172, read through indexed primary PDF extracts. Direct PDF retrieval failed. Exact reproducible queries: "Gaomiaoshan" "Chen Yanbin" for p. 133, and site.ihp.sinica.edu.tw "Gaomiaoshan" "no" "date" for p. 141. Other indexed passages support family membership and monastic teaching titles. Dating relies on style and place names, not an explicit dated dedication.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Buddhist stele dedicated by Helian Ziyue, 533-543
sources.note: Direct object record 29.72. A devotional society of 500, named historical patron, Vimalakirti-Manjushri debate, ink rubbings and possible later recarving are explicit. Date range straddles the Northern Wei/Eastern Wei transition.

sources.title: Cleveland Museum of Art, Stele of Shakyamuni and Bodhisattvas, 537
sources.note: Direct collection record 1914.567, inscription, donor Yuan’ning and deceased consort, Hebei attribution and surviving pigment. A specific elite family memorial, not a universal family custom.

sources.title: Princeton University Art Museum, Buddhist stone stele, 535
sources.note: Direct object record 2020-686. Inscription partly obscured by robe, Tianping year 2 converted to 535, combination of clerical and regular scripts, and names of donors. No unviewed Chinese date text is reconstructed.

sources.title: Asian Art Museum, Standing figure of a Central Asian, 534-550
sources.note: Direct object B60P1629. Painted earthenware, Hebei, 21 cm; identification expressly tentative in museum description. Broader Han-to-Tang discussion on the page is not evidence for individual Eastern Wei communities.

sources.title: Tsz Shan Monastery Buddhist Art Museum, Standing Guanyin Bodhisattva, 545
sources.note: Direct English collection record and corresponding Chinese page read. Object 2017.05; Wuding year 3, monk Daohe and devotees, pale stone, ring fastening and folded drapery. No modern reconstruction of an inscription is quoted.

proposedOverrides.summary: A northern Chinese state governed by the Gao family behind an emperor at Ye.

index.name: Eastern Wei
index.summary: The eastern half of the Northern Wei after the court split in 534, ruled from Ye by the general Gao Huan behind a puppet emperor.

fell.text: Gao Yang deposed the last Eastern Wei emperor in 550 and founded the Northern Qi.

properties.note: coarse extent drawn by the site after Tan Qixiang's Historical Atlas of China; not a surveyed border

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact historical index record, 534-550. No aliases or other Wei/Qi dynasties absorbed. Northern Qi is the identified historical successor already present in the index.
limitations: Site-created coarse China-seams polygon is not a surveyed border; the public opening says so.
Qimin yaoshu is a contemporary regional knowledge source compiled 533-544, not a proven state commission.
Helian Ziyue’s stele dates 533-543 and explicitly straddles the Northern/Eastern Wei boundary.
Gaomiaoshan is assigned to Eastern Wei by scholarly analysis, without an exact dated dedication. No artificial exact year is attached.
Specific donors, royal families and farming advice are not generalized into universal household, education or health provision. No unsupported medicine or sanitation system supplied.
No Princess Linhe/Ruru tomb used; that material is reserved for the Rouran researcher.
